summary: Jackson County Forest Service fire tower on the Shawnee; staffed in 1949, listed for sale in 1972, now gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: steel fire tower built by the Forest Service (1972 sale notice refers to it as a steel lookout tower)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association and marked removed on the Central US Lookouts page; no removal date is given.

events.note: A description written about 1942 calls it a fire tower constructed by the Forest Service for fire detection, with a scenic view of the surrounding country from the cab.
A two-day hiking route was laid out beginning at the tower, seven miles southwest of Murphysboro.
A forester was at the top of the tower during a June 1949 forest tour; the tower was one of 15 protecting 475,000 acres within the Shawnee area.
Bids advertised in the Southern Illinoisan to sell this and seven other steel lookout towers on the Shawnee National Forest.

notes_for_editor: Name collision: the Hickory Ridge Fire Tower in Indiana (Hoosier National Forest, Monroe County, 1936 CCC build, standing) is a different structure and is the source of the 1936 date in some listings; do not attribute it to the Illinois tower. No source gives this tower's construction date, and no source describes what remains at the site. The record's agency (Shawnee National Forest) is supported by the page heading 'Jackson County - Shawnee National Forest'. No access level is stated in any source, so access is left out. No photo found.
